_comment: Moons of Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Orbits: JPL Solar System Dynamics, 'Planetary Satellite Mean Elements', https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/sats/elem/ (retrieved 2026-10-06). Sizes: JPL 'Planetary Satellite Physical Parameters', https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/sats/phys_par/ (retrieved 2026-10-06); only the larger moons have a measured mean radius (null otherwise). Earth's Moon is not listed here (the page uses its own circular-orbit model) and Pluto's moons are left out because Pluto is not drawn. Fields copied unchanged: a (km), e, w = argument of periapsis (deg), M = mean anomaly at epoch (deg), i = inclination to the reference plane (deg, > 90 means retrograde), node (deg), P = sidereal period (days), frame = reference plane of the elements, epoch (TDB). The page draws these orbits flat and approximate (longitude of periapsis taken as node + w).
source: JPL Solar System Dynamics planetary satellite mean elements and physical parameters (NASA/JPL-Caltech)
